speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To better understand the cause of your acute diarrhea, how many bowel movements have you had in the last 24 hours, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very high frequency of bowel movements, and given your recent treatment with levofloxacin, we must consider *Clostridioides difficile* infection. Have you experienced any fever, chills, or nausea alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: *Clostridioides difficile* infection. REQUEST TEST: Stool C. difficile toxin assay. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal X-ray.
